# Contacts & Search

One of the most used pages in Levitate is the Contacts People page. When you navigate from the Dashboard to the Contact's button in the navigation menu, you'll first get taken to People. There, all contacts will show. These contacts can be sorted and filtered, and actions such as emailing, merging, texting, starting automations, and more can be initiated.

## What you'll see on the People page

From the People page, you can choose Table Settings from the right-hand navigation bar. From there, you'll be able to choose which fields will display in up to eight columns on the People page— Name is always required, and you can also choose to see Tags, Contact, Info, Creation Date, Job Title, Birthday, Anniversary, Age, Contact Owner, and Last Communication. Once you choose up to eight of these fields, your People page will always show those choices, but you can change them and update them as often as you'd like.

Here's the selected menu for columns:

![](https://d33v4339jhl8k0.cloudfront.net/docs/assets/602c2dafc6b4255ec1783588/images/69f26f930ed955013b8755a6/file-SSLv744BMc.png)

View of the People page with multiple columns selected:

![](https://d33v4339jhl8k0.cloudfront.net/docs/assets/602c2dafc6b4255ec1783588/images/6a35615f248aacc99479a317/file-psW1aNgGAF.png)

In Levitate, users can search by tag groups, name, email address, company, and multiple statuses, key facts, and dates.

## Filtering Contacts

To get more granular in your search, such as by a renewal date or a review date, click the filter icon (tooltip: **Filter contacts**) in the toolbar on the right-hand side of the Contacts page to open the filter panel.

From there, you'll see a multitude of options when searching:

![](https://d33v4339jhl8k0.cloudfront.net/docs/assets/602c2dafc6b4255ec1783588/images/6a35615e671870169720ecef/file-B0sxd93i28.png)

### Filter by Key Fact

![](https://d33v4339jhl8k0.cloudfront.net/docs/assets/602c2dafc6b4255ec1783588/images/69f26f92d7a0d11cccffadde/0Lwl22d7u7ofhEG6VigRM-G-dh6jDIUy6NAwWUh8wciekgZzmPvOO1qB-G_EXaAJ6TMx2gnvH4fwXa8LHGr4mJVpGr92jF9005yUyTlGE62ZUz1E-bBUInJj-LbC.png)

You're also able to search by a status, or by multiple intersecting statuses, like contacts without an email address or contacts that have an alert due for outreach!

You are able to filter contacts by ownership— users can choose to see All contacts (all Shared contacts), the contacts that they own, contacts owned by a specific other user, or contacts that they have a connection with.

### Filter by Tags

Upon choosing 'advanced search' users are able to search by a tag or by multiple, intersecting, tag groups. Tags can also be excluded! What this looks like:

![](https://d33v4339jhl8k0.cloudfront.net/docs/assets/602c2dafc6b4255ec1783588/images/69f26f94a55fdb4084444270/zZOWCmI5DWFMYQbBisZBbbXO6vDZJe6dZiGeG3DR3L4NX_Wis5woWH7jcJPcFbHi6CpnAsDNHXBnostzwZWV3bxwNVVgJf5zLdDKek_LmRkE3nHvjiNh-LsveOB7.png)

### Searching a specific age range or by upcoming birthdays

As of July 2024, users are able to search by a specific age range (data pulled from contact birthday key facts) and by upcoming birthdates. This feature can be used for a number of reasons, like searching for clients that are eligible for Medicare or retirement information based on age.

![](https://d33v4339jhl8k0.cloudfront.net/docs/assets/602c2dafc6b4255ec1783588/images/69f26f92ece9afe68bb7fac0/AD_4nXelXasOuU2eCXv1ADV3yNPVZ36H-MqxwEUSAPyEyUmDtX1Bb7umVyYgtRngLO-mOZGqXx0cvfZNWCnHEkJKlwLuF2T3rvyZCDLqE_syNkw_Th03SVSw6tPu.png)

_Searching by age range_

![](https://d33v4339jhl8k0.cloudfront.net/docs/assets/602c2dafc6b4255ec1783588/images/69f26f925e6a7b6a1f76cfdb/AD_4nXcHdgdyCgiB1B-OotiOL981ihrD-P8Bq6EBEde-ffclJX7Id-oUHYHNcUzF_nIwLdt-5YILiEHi3sF_OtSsvYZecE85QEWLqRHVh-Nl5AtY9gPCmD9VHh8N.png)

_Searching by a range of birthdates_

### Filtering by Creation Date

Levitate makes the date that the contact was created (added to) in Levitate\* on the Contact page. You are able to sort from the main contact view, and sort by creation dates in Advanced Search.

![](https://d33v4339jhl8k0.cloudfront.net/docs/assets/602c2dafc6b4255ec1783588/images/69f26f93ece9afe68bb7fac1/file-4cR1UKkn5D.png)

\*To reiterate— the Creation Date is the date that the contact was added to Levitate— not the date they were created in or added to another source system.

### Saved Searches

Once you've applied at least one filter, a **Save Search** link appears above the contact list, next to the description of your active filters. Click it, name the search, and save!

To use a saved search, open the filter panel with the filter icon in the right-hand toolbar, then expand **Saved Searches**. Click a saved search to apply its filters (including its ownership filter). To delete a saved search, click the remove button next to it.

### Searching by Age vs. Searching by Birthdate

In the Advanced Search feature, users are able to search both by Age (as in 'Turning XX Years') and Birthdate (which ignores year and focuses on Month/Date.)

### Last Communication Filter

Users are able to filter and search by 'Last Communication.' The criteria is just based on the most recent to least recent point of contact with a specific contact.

### Filter by City, State, or Zip

Users are able to filter and search by a contact's listed City, State, or Zip Code.

### Filter by Company Tag

This allows Company Tags to be searched for in reference to Contacts within a Company, using a new Advanced Filter option in Contacts and Campaigns. This filter will look at the contacts associated with a company.

### Filter by Custom Field

Contact advanced search now supports filtering by custom field values. In the filter panel, choose **Custom Field** to see a searchable dropdown of your account's custom fields. Select a field, then enter the value you want to match. This filter is available on the Contacts page and in the audience selection flow for email, text, and handwritten card campaigns.

### Filter by SMS Status

On accounts with texting enabled, the contact filter panel includes two SMS status checkboxes:

- **Can receive text** — contacts who have not opted out of SMS and are eligible to receive text messages.
- **Opted out of text** — contacts who have unsubscribed from SMS messages.

### Filter by Job Title

The advanced search panel includes a **Job Title** filter. Enter any text to find contacts whose job title starts with that value — for example, typing "Dir" returns contacts with titles like "Director" or "Director of Operations." This lets you segment contacts by role without needing a separate tag for each title.

The filter is available in both the People page filter drawer and the recipient picker when composing a campaign. Searches saved with a job title criterion and automation triggers also support this filter.

## Duplicate Contacts

Levitate does not have an automatic bulk duplicate scanner, so finding duplicates is a manual process. Use one of the search methods below to surface potential duplicates, then merge the records you identify. For step-by-step merge instructions see [Merging Contacts by ID instead of email address](https://help.levitate.ai/article/334-contact-merging-id-email).

### Method 1: Search by Email Address

The most reliable way to find duplicates is to search by a shared email address.

1. Go to Contacts page
2. Enter email address to Search bar to check for duplicates.
3. View all contacts with that email address.
4. Manually Merge contacts if duplicates are found.

#### Finding Common Email Duplicates

- Search your domain email (@company.com)
- Check personal emails (gmail.com, yahoo.com)
- Look for common patterns (info@, admin@, contact@)

### Method 2: Search by Last Name

Find potential duplicates that share the same last name.

1. Go to Contacts page
2. Use search bar at top
3. Enter Last Name
4. Sort results alphabetically
5. Visually scan for duplicate first names
6. Check email addresses to confirm

### Method 3: Export and Analyze in Spreadsheet

For a more systematic duplicate scan, export your contacts and analyze them outside Levitate.

1. Contacts page > Select All > Export to CSV
2. Open in Excel/Google Sheets
3. Sort by Email Address column
4. Look for consecutive rows with same email
5. Sort by Last Name + First Name
6. Identify duplicates manually
7. Return to Levitate to merge identified duplicates

### Method 4: Filter by Import Date

After a CSV import, check whether any duplicates were created.

1. Advanced Search > Date Added
2. Select import date range
3. Review new contacts
4. Cross-reference with existing contacts by email
5. Merge duplicates found

### Reactive Duplicate Detection

When you manually create a contact whose email address already belongs to an existing contact, Levitate shows a warning with a **Show Duplicates** button for about 10 seconds (when duplicate contacts are enabled for your account). Click it to view all contacts sharing that email, then choose which record to keep and merge.

### Best Practices for Preventing Duplicates

#### During Import

- Levitate matches on email address to prevent duplicates
- Clean data before import (remove obvious duplicates in CSV)
- Use Additional ID field for contacts sharing emails to intentionally create duplicates (household members)

#### During Manual Entry

- Always enter email address (triggers duplicate detection)
- Watch for the **Show Duplicates** button
- Review before creating new contact

#### Ongoing Maintenance to prevent overlap

- Monthly duplicate audits using Method 1 or 3
- Standardize data entry (name formats, email formats)
- Train team on duplicate prevention

### Merging Duplicates

Once you have identified duplicates, merge them directly from the Contacts (People) page:

1. On the People page, select the checkboxes next to two or more duplicate contacts.
2. In the actions bar that appears, click **Merge**.
3. In the merge wizard, select the contact record you want to keep as the primary record.
4. Click **Merge** to confirm. Data from both records is combined and the duplicate is removed.

**Note:** For contacts that share the same email address but need to remain separate (for example, household members), use an Additional ID to keep them from merging. See [Merging Contacts by ID instead of email address](https://help.levitate.ai/article/334-contact-merging-id-email) for details.

### Limitations

Levitate does not provide an automated bulk duplicate scanner. Duplicate detection is manual — you need to search by email address or name to identify potential duplicates, then merge them one group at a time. The export-and-spreadsheet method (Method 3 above) is the most efficient approach when auditing a large contact list.

## Companies

Companies under the 'Company' tab on the Contacts page are populated by domains associated with contacts. Users with common company domains will be grouped under the umbrella of a company.

Don't want to see companies? Reach out to Support or your Success specialist and visibility for the company tab can be turned off in Settings > Administrative.

The Companies page supports advanced tag filtering with OR, AND, and NOT logic via a filter drawer — the same filter experience available on the People page. Open the filter drawer from the Companies tab to search by one or more tags, combine multiple criteria, or exclude specific tags. This makes it easy to segment companies the same way you segment individual contacts.

The search box on the Companies tab has a search-type dropdown to its left with three options: **All**, **Name**, and **Tag**. The dropdown is always visible and defaults to **All**, so a plain search matches tags as well as company names. Choose **Name** to match company names only, or **Tag** to match tags only. If you change the search type while a search is active, the search runs again with the new type. Clicking **Clear search** resets the search type to **All**.

## FAQs

**Q: How do I do a bulk scan for duplicate contacts and then merge them?**

A: Levitate does not have an automatic bulk duplicate finder. The most thorough approach is to export your contact list to a CSV (Contacts page > select contacts > Export), then sort the spreadsheet by email address or by last name and first name to find matching rows. Once you have identified a set of duplicates, return to Levitate, select the duplicate contacts on the People page, and click **Merge** in the actions bar. For full merge instructions, including how to handle contacts that share an email address on purpose, see [Merging Contacts by ID instead of email address](https://help.levitate.ai/article/334-contact-merging-id-email).

**Q: Why am I able to see contacts when they are set to private?**

A: If you're able to view a contact that is marked as private, it's likely because you are listed as a connection on that contact. Connections can still access contacts they're associated with, even if those contacts are set to private and owned by another user.

**Q: What is the best practice to avoid duplicate contacts when connecting or switching to a new integration database?**

A: The only reliable way to avoid duplicates when connecting to a new integration database is to wipe your existing Levitate contacts before the integration is connected, then let the new integration sync in a clean set of records. Contacts that come in through an integration cannot be merged after the fact, so any duplicates created at sync time will need to be cleaned up at the source system. If you're switching integrations or connecting one for the first time, contact your Success Specialist before you begin — they'll help you wipe the account safely and coordinate the new sync.

**Note:** The Merge Contacts feature does not work on contacts that originated from an integration, which is why wiping the account before connecting is the recommended approach.

**Q: Why does my email campaign show fewer contacts with email addresses than the total number of contacts in my tag?**

A: When you select a tag as your campaign audience, Levitate shows two numbers: the total contacts in that tag and, separately, how many of those contacts have an email address on record. The difference reflects contacts that cannot receive the campaign email for one or more of the following reasons: the contact has no email address stored in Levitate; the contact has previously unsubscribed from emails; or the contact's email address has bounced in the past. Only contacts that have a valid, contactable email address are counted in the "contacts with email addresses" figure shown before you send.
